62364.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62364.question_text: Investors in a business are mainly interested in firm's--------
62364.explanation: The most important thing investors want to see in a firm it invested in is the return on their investment, investors are mostly interested in how profitable a business venture is.

62365.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62365.question_text: One of the characteristics of useful accounting information is--------
62365.explanation: The four major qualitative characteristics of useful accounting information are comparability, verifiability, timeliness, and understandability.

62463.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62463.question_text: Which of the following items is found on the debit side of the trial balance?
62463.explanation: It has our assets, expenses, and drawings on the left (the debit side). The discount allowed is an expense and it is posted on the debit side of the trial balance.

62464.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62464.question_text: Which of the following transactions is a revenue expenditure?
62464.explanation: Revenue expenditures are short-term expenses used in the current period or typically within one year. It includes the expenses required to meet the ongoing operational costs of running a business. Option D is correct.

62465.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62465.question_text: Credit notes received are source documents for.........
62465.explanation: Credit notes are given to a buyer/customer by the seller for goods returned. Since the goods are returned to the seller, it is recorded in the returns inwards journal.

62467.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62467.question_text: A document forwarded to a supplier showing unsatisfactory goods is................................

62469.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62469.question_text: The claim of a proprietor of a business entity on its assets is................
62469.explanation: Drawings is the money withdrawn from a business by its owners for personal use. A drawing account is used primarily for businesses that are taxed as sole proprietorships or partnerships.

62470.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62470.question_text: The apportionment of the cost of a fixed asset to the profit and loss account is termed?

62471.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62471.question_text: Entries in the purchase journal are transferred to the .............
62471.explanation:
The purchase journal records all credit purchases. All the entries are then moved to the accounts payable. 

Accounts payable are amounts due to vendors or suppliers for goods or services received that have not yet been paid for.

62472.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62472.question_text: A reduction n price to encourage prompt payment is........
62472.explanation: Cash discounts refer to an incentive that a seller offers to a buyer in return for paying a bill before the scheduled due date. The seller would typically reduce a certain amount from the total amount owed to encourage the buyer to make payment faster.

62473.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62473.question_text:
Tei Ltd offered 1,560 units of magazines at N60 each. Trade discount is 10%  and cash discount is 10% within 30 days and 5% within 60 days.

The cash discount allowed on the 50th day is?

62474.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62474.question_text:
Tei Ltd offered 1,560 units of magazines at N60 each. Trade discount is 10%  and cash discount is 10% within 30 days and 5% within 60 days.

The amount payable if payment is made on the 40th day is...........

62475.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62475.question_text: An amount of Le2000 received from a customer, Koffi has been credited to another customer, Kofigo's account. This is an error of?
62475.explanation:
Error of commission is an error that occurs when doing something wrong, such as including a wrong amount or including an amount in the wrong place.

For example, money that has been received from a customer is credited properly to the accounts receivable account, but to the wrong customer.

62476.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62476.question_text: The current assets less current liabilities is
62476.explanation:
The working capital in simple terms is the money used in the day-to-day running of the business.

It is the difference between a company's current assets—such as cash, accounts receivable, inventories of raw materials, and finished goods—and its current liabilities, such as accounts payable and debts.

62478.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62478.question_text: A debit balance of N420 on the purchase ledger control account means that as at that date............
62478.explanation: The purchase ledger control account is part of the balance sheet and shows at any given time how much you owe to your suppliers. It is credited if its balance increases & debited if its balance decreases.

options.text: trade creditors have been paid by N420
goods returned to trade creditors amounted to N420
total supplies from trade creditors amounted to N420

62492.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62492.question_text: Sales and purchases ledger are used in a business to keep records of?

options.text: the owner's capital and cash transactions
accounts of individual customers and suppliers
current liabilities and long term liabilities

62495.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62495.question_text: Which of the following activities will increase profits?
62495.explanation:
The provision for doubtful debts is the estimated amount of bad debt that will arise from accounts receivable (credit sales) that have been issued but not yet collected.

If a business estimated 20,000 as bad debts, a reduction to a lesser amount means the business will make more money from sales, which amounts to higher profits.

options.text: reduction in provision for doubtful debts

62497.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62497.question_text: The concept that implies that a business will operate for an indefinitely long period of time is...............
62497.explanation: The going concern concept is an accounting term that states that a business entity will continue running its operations in the foreseeable future and will not be liquidated or forced to discontinue operations for any reason.

62580.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62580.explanation: The concept of consistency means that accounting methods once adopted must be applied consistently in the future, and same methods and techniques must be used for similar situations

options.text: ensuring that all expenses are matched against revenue

62581.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62581.question_text: The concept which states that revenue is recognized when goods are sold is
62581.explanation: The realization concept states that revenue can only be recognized once the available goods or services associated with the revenue have been delivered or sold.

62583.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62583.question_text: Cost of goods sold is calculated as...................
62583.explanation: Starting inventory + purchases − ending inventory = cost of goods sold

62586.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62586.question_text: The wages of an office cleaner is classified as
62586.explanation: Administrative overhead is those costs not involved in the development or production of goods or services. Administrative overhead is those costs not involved in the development or production of goods or services.

62590.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62590.question_text:
Use the information below to answer the question that follows

Sales--------------- 120,000
Purchase-----------100,000
Opening stock-----10,000
Closing stock------20,000

The cost of goods sold is-----------
62590.explanation:
Cost of goods sold = opening stock + purchase - closing stock

10,000 + 100,000 - 20,000 = 90,000

Purchase-----------100,000

The gross profit or loss is?
62595.explanation:

62599.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62599.question_text: The amount set aside out of profits to strengthen the financial position of the business is
62599.explanation: A reserve is profits that have been appropriated for a particular purpose. Reserves are sometimes set up to purchase fixed assets, pay an expected legal settlement, pay bonuses, pay off debt, pay for repairs and maintenance, and so forth.

62631.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62631.question_text: A fall in the value of a fixed asset due to technological changes is described as?
62631.explanation: Obsolescence is a process by which a machine, or in this case, a fixed asset becomes outdated, no longer used or losses value as a result of changes in the level of technology.

62632.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62632.question_text: A credit entry is made in the plant and machinery account for the ......................

options.text: purchase of an additional plant and machinery

62633.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62633.explanation: Royalty paid on the basis of output (manufacturing) is debited to the Trading or Manufacturing Account as it is considered a normal business expenditure.

options.text: credited to the profit and loss account

62634.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62634.question_text: One of the components of factory overhead is............
62634.explanation:
Costs that support production but are not direct materials or direct labor are considered overhead. It includes;

  • Depreciation of equipment and factory facilities.
  • Rent, property taxes, insurance, and utilities.
  • Employment costs for supervisors, maintenance and quality control staff, and any other on-site employees who aren't physically making signs.

62635.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62635.question_text:
Use the following information to answer the question that follows

                                                       N
Direct material used-----------------64,000
Direct labour--------------------------30,000
Production overheads--------------22,000
Work-in-progress at beginning-----9,000
Work-in-progress at close---------14,000

Prime cost of production is?
62635.explanation:
Prime cost = Direct materials cost + Direct labor cost

64,000 + 30,000 = 94,000

62636.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62636.question_text:
Use the following information to answer the question that follows

                                                       N
Direct material used-----------------64,000
Direct labour--------------------------30,000
Production overheads--------------22,000
Work-in-progress at beginning-----9,000
Work-in-progress at close---------14,000

The total cost of production is
62636.explanation:
Total cost of production = Cost of labor + Cost of raw materials + Overhead costs on manufacturing.

64,000 + 30,000 + 22,000 = 116,000

62637.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62637.question_text: The balance on the sales ledger control account at the end of the accounting year represents a total.........
62637.explanation: A sales ledger control account, also called trade debtors control, is the part of your balance sheet that displays how much your customers owe the company.

amount transferred from the sales journal

62641.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62641.question_text: The excess of assets over liabilities in a not for profit organization is--------------
62641.explanation: Accumulated fund is the excess money received by a non-profit organization. It is gotten by deducting liabilities from assets in a non-profit making organization account.

62642.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62642.question_text: The parties who are paid last in the event of winding-up are
62642.explanation: Ordinary Shareholders represent people who have a fraction of ownership in a corporation that issues such shares. They get to vote on the company's major decisions, usually decided at its shareholder meetings. The shareholder may or may not receive a dividend. They are usually the last to get paid in the event that the company is folding up.

62649.explanation: An allotment of shares is when a company distributes newly bought shares to applicants.

62655.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62655.question_text: The authority to incur expenditure in the public sector is-------------

62656.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
62656.question_text: ''Below the line'' item in public sector accounting means such an item is--------
62656.explanation:
In public sector accounting, an item categorized as ''below the line'' is an income or expense in accounting which have no noticeable effect on company profits in the current period.

It means the item does not affect the profit or loss from normal operations for that accounting period.

options.text: not budgeted for in the current fiscal year
less than what is budgeted for
budgeted for in the current fiscal year
to be carried forward to the next fiscal year
